review.assessment: I checked the source against the approved Requirements3 and Design2 and the unchanged prior code; I found no source, regression or false-credit defect. Production code. The Engine retry guard (`actor != EvidencePort && dispatch_started && session_id.is_none()`) runs after the Waiting/Failed admission and before the irreversible check, the Session loop and every in-memory mutation, so Running/Interrupted/Evaluating keep their existing refusal. The Store guard sits inside the existing `before.active.is_some() && after.active != before.active` closure block. It runs after validate_transition and before the Session scan, context validation/insert, put_task_tx/put_record_tx and audit. `before.history[before.active.unwrap()]` is guarded by that condition and mirrors the existing own_id indexing. It exempts only TerminalRecovery, whose earlier conservative fence applies the same predicate. Both refusals use the single crate-private literal, and anyhow's ensure renders it verbatim through persist without added context, so Engine-only removal really is indistinguishable. The owner's fail() and Session binding and TerminalDecision keep active and never enter the block. release_preparation and pre-marker invalidations carry marker=false. Bound or port completions, retries and invalidations fail the predicate. TerminalRecovery still refuses through its original fence. No legitimate production closure changes; the only rewritten test is the characterization rename. Controls. The FakeAgent change keeps the default start_error path identical. The matching-row variant persists a terminal Failed same-scope/agent/role Executor Session before Err, which passes validate_worktree_exclusion. full_snapshot reads every row and column of projects, goals, tasks, records, context_versions, usage and audit in stable order, plus both launch counters. The generation_builder satisfies validate_transition and validate_context (invalidate, then next_phase after invalidate, the same sources, the new generation, task.context_version+1 equal to the latest pointer here, then set_context). The pre-marker commits for both actors at offsets 3 and 4 independently validate both builders. At offset 3 the stale owner fails in refresh_owners and release_preparation; at offset 4 its marker persist fails untyped in validate_transition. The test asserts only that the full post-closure snapshot and counters are unchanged, which is correct. Held marked Running refusals cover StateOnly retry and generation closures for both actors and ReadOnly/Mutating for the Executor; the original owner then binds or publishes Failed on the same index with no extra launch. TerminalDecision keeps active, and the resumed owner's fail is rejected by the terminal-Task fence with an unchanged snapshot. The positives (pre-marker repair with exactly one fresh launch per actor, bound review rejection, port Waiting/Failed) are reached through the real step paths. Mutation accounting matches the patches and excerpts. Every credited kill is behavioural: unwrap_err on a committed Ok at unbound_retry.rs:152/209/268, unwrap on a wrongful refusal at 440/564, or the original Issue41 tests.rs:4195 unwrap_err and 4166 is_err. None depends on text differences. That gives 17 unique operators (15 new plus 2 re-executed Issue41), with M01f correctly counted as the same operator. M08 and M22 break normal completion inside Fixture::through and are correctly given no credit. The distinct retry-outcome-scoped M08b and M22b kill at the real retry. The masked, equivalent and survivor classifications (M14 to M18) are accurate. The impact inventory is consistent with source: the only production transition writers are persist, reserve and persist_decision, the other direct writer is observe_workflow_gate, put_record rejects Workflow, and the new CodexAdapter has empty capabilities, so the capability check fails it before the marker. The Generic and Grok start-error split matches. Scope is respected: no schema, API, bypass, certificate, producer, timeout or permission change, and no whole Issue14, native, F1 or MVP claim. The remaining finding is the Low wording and Issue14-publication gate item; final current-head CI identity is still required before merge, as the packet already states.

review.assessment: I checked the source against approved Requirements3/Design2 and the current tested code bytes. Production change: the Engine `retry` guard runs after the Waiting/Failed admission and before the irreversible check, the Session loop and every in-memory mutation. It uses the exact predicate (actor != EvidencePort && dispatch_started && session_id None) and the shared crate-private literal. The Store guard sits inside the existing original-active closure block (`before.active.is_some() && after.active != before.active`). It runs after validate_transition and before the Session scan, context insert, Task/Record CAS and audit, and is keyed on the DB `before` attempt with `access != TerminalRecovery`. TerminalRecovery is still refused earlier by the conservative fence on the same attempt, and TerminalDecision, the owner's Running→Failed publication and Session binding keep active, so they never enter the block. A refusal rolls back the immediate transaction, and the caller's structs are assigned only after commit. Enumerated production closures are unaffected: release_preparation and pre-marker invalidations carry marker=false; bound and EvidencePort completions, retries and invalidations have a Session or are EvidencePort. The only existing assertion change is the renamed characterization test. The new Codex implementor cannot produce marked-unbound attempts in the Workflow: its capabilities are empty, so prepare_agent fails before the marker, and its start refuses at Availability::require. Controls are causal and correctly constructed. Both actors' held starts reach Failed with the marker set and no Session (Executor: no Session rows; Reviewer: the Exited Implement executor row). Public retry refuses, a later step does not replay, and the full raw all-table snapshot plus both launch counters stays unchanged. The direct Failed and matching-terminal-row closures refuse. The matching row is a terminal Failed executor row, which is admitted today by both the Engine Session loop and the Store closing loop, so only the new fences refuse it. On held marked Running, StateOnly retry and generation builders refuse, and ReadOnly and Mutating closures refuse (the Executor has no Session rows, so those scans pass). The released owner then binds once or publishes Failed on the same index, and TerminalDecision keeps active, after which the stale owner's fail is rejected and nothing changes. The identical builders commit on pre-marker Running at offsets 3 and 4 for both actors. At offset 3 the stale owner fails refresh_owners and its release; at offset 4 it fails validate_transition untyped at marker publication. In both cases there is no write, audit row or launch. The builders also commit on the pre-marker definitive Failed, bound terminal review-rejection and port Waiting/Failed fixtures. Public pre-marker repair, bound and port retries keep their RetryEvent, active=None and single-launch behaviour. The mutation ledger matches the patches and consumers: 25 executions, 18 assertion kills (17 unique operators), 5 correctly classified survivors and 2 broad Store setup failures without credit. Every kill comes from an actual Ok/Err effect: `unwrap_err` on a committed `Ok`, or `unwrap` on a wrongly refused supported retry. No kill relies on message text. Engine-only removal stays masked by the shared literal. Issue41's single and combined TerminalRecovery mutants still commit with the exemption in place. No schema, public API, bypass, certificate, timeout or permission change is introduced. Only the Low wording finalization remains. I make no whole-Issue14, native, F1 or MVP claim.
